The statement signals a modestly dovish tilt: the FOMC lowered the target range by 25 bps to 4.5–4.75% and cut the interest on reserve balances to 4.65%, while continuing quantitative tightening (Treasury runoff capped at $25B/month and MBS paydowns reinvested into Treasuries above a $35B cap). In New Keynesian/DSGE frameworks used by central banks, the stance hinges on the expected real policy rate relative to the natural rate; with inflation “somewhat elevated” but easing, a small nominal cut can still leave policy mildly restrictive in real terms, consistent with stabilizing inflation while cushioning growth. VAR and empirical literature (Eichenbaum, Sims, Zha) imply such easing supports real activity with lags, while the credit channel (Bernanke, Gertler, Gilchrist) suggests lower short rates can ease financing conditions—partly offset by ongoing balance-sheet runoff. The Committee’s “risks roughly in balance” language aligns with flexible inflation-forecast targeting (Svensson) and a Phillips-curve-based, data-dependent approach, while the emphasis on returning inflation to 2% reflects the well-documented welfare costs of inflation (Friedman; Phelps; Ireland/Dotsey). Netting these, the communication is slightly positive for the outlook and risk assets, but tempered by uncertainty and continued QT.
